content.text: I now understand the full system. Let me implement. Starting with the server-side secrets module.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The test stack's /worker (design/test-stack-image.md) — the ROOT flake's
# #caosImage is this image, so this is the one /worker the caos tree itself
# defines. It is an interpreter in the flake-images.md sense (read the next
# executable from `worker1` and run it), except that before running it, it
# brings up a COMPLETE caos stack built from the tree under test, inside this
# container.
#
# TWO CAOSES LIVE HERE:
#   /bin/caos     the setuid gateway the HOST composed as this image's caos
#                 additions — this image's own worker-side client, talking to
#                 the OUTER stack. It is what the ambient environment
#                 resolves to, and what every `caos` in THIS script is.
#   /caos/bin/*   what the tree under test built. These go on PATH for
#                 worker1 ONLY, at the call site.
#
# Keeping them straight is TWO independent choices, and both matter:
#
#   which BINARY   whose semantics and protocol you speak. The outer server
#                  and runnerd are the host's, so outer work must use the
#                  host's client; the tested client is the thing under test
#                  and may differ from it in any way at all — that is the
#                  point of building it. Do not assume they are interchangeable
#                  because they happen to agree today.
#   which URL      which server that binary then talks to. Both clients read
#                  the same CAOS_SERVER_URL (one variable, different values:
#                  the runner injects the outer server's address, $INNER is
#                  the stack below), so the env alone does not say which
#                  client is running.
#
# Getting the binary right and the URL wrong fails loudly: /bin/caos under the
# flipped env asks the INNER server for an outer object and 404s (measured).
# Getting the URL right and the binary wrong fails SILENTLY — a host client
# driving the test stack passes until the tree under test changes the client,
# and then it tests the wrong thing.
#
# Both are safe here by construction rather than by discipline:
#   - /caos/bin is never on the ambient PATH (the image sets PATH=/bin), so
#     nothing in this script can reach the tested client by accident;
#   - worker1 never needs an outer client, because the args are materialized
#     below before the env flips and its /tmp/out is published after, so it
#     has no outer work left to do with the wrong one.
#
# The inner runnerd delegates every worker to the OUTER engine through the
# granted socket, as siblings sharing this container's netns — no second
# nesting level (design/cargo-workers.md, phase 4). NOBODY publishes std at
# runtime: this tree's own build-builtins.sh published it once, when the image
# was built, and the caller hands that result in as an arg (the seed below).
#
# What the image lays out for worker1, all fixed paths:
#   /caos/bin       the binaries a STACK needs (caos, caos-cli, server,
#                   runnerd), so the caos every inner image carries is the
#                   tested one. The WORKER binaries are NOT here — they ride in
#                   the caller's wrapper, per job, so that editing one does not
#                   move this image and re-key every test that runs it.
#   /caos/stack     the one bring-up
set -euo pipefail

LOGS="/tmp/serve.log /tmp/redis.log /tmp/server.log /tmp/runnerd.log"
fail() {
  echo "TEST STACK FAIL: $*" >&2
  for l in $LOGS; do
    [ -e "$l" ] || continue
    echo "--- $l" >&2
    cat "$l" >&2
  done
  exit 1
}

# Materialize EVERY arg while the environment is still the outer one. This is
# what makes the call-site env flip below sufficient: worker1 runs entirely
# in the inner world and never needs the outer stack, because both clients
# read the same CAOS_SERVER_URL and a `caos get` under the flipped env would
# ask the INNER server for an outer object (it 404s — measured).
caos get -r /cas/args

# The OUTER run's std and salt must not reach the inner client (the phase-3
# isolation lesson). Scrubbed here, so nothing worker1 starts inherits them.
unset CAOS_STD CAOS_SALT

SOCK=${CAOS_ENGINE_SOCKET:?the test stack needs a granted engine socket}
[ -S "$SOCK" ] || fail "engine socket $SOCK is not a socket"

INNER=http://127.0.0.1

# ---- the seed, from the CALLER's std ----------------------------------------
# std used to be baked into this image (/caos/seed-git), which meant the image
# moved whenever any worker binary did, and every test re-keyed on every worker
# edit. It arrives as an arg instead, and the caller hands each job only the
# entries that job uses (caos-tools/test.sh, stage3) — so what re-keys a test is
# what the test actually reaches for.
#
# Seeding is a git FETCH of the tree's closure from the outer server, not a
# publish: build-builtins already did the expensive half (building and pushing
# the core images) once, at image build time, and the registry still holds it.
# What is left is moving a few objects. Measured on the whole of std, 9.3 MB:
# 0.69s; per entry 73-250ms. That is why this can be per-stack again.
#
# It has to happen HERE, before the env flips, because $CAOS_SERVER_URL is the
# outer server only until then.
STD_HASH=$(caos hash /cas/args/in/std) || fail "no std in the wrapper — the caller hands each job the entries it uses"
SEED=/tmp/seed-git
git init -q --bare "$SEED" || fail "creating the seed repo"
git -c fetch.negotiationAlgorithm=noop -C "$SEED" fetch -q --no-write-fetch-head \
  "$CAOS_SERVER_URL" "$STD_HASH" \
  || fail "fetching std $STD_HASH from the outer server"
git -C "$SEED" update-ref refs/caos/std "$STD_HASH" \
  || fail "pointing refs/caos/std at $STD_HASH"

# The inner stack itself is `caosd serve` (design/one-stack-image.md) — the
# ONE bring-up in the tree, shared with the host and seed placements, so this
# script no longer carries a second copy of how a stack starts. What stays
# here is what only this placement knows:
#
#   - the result cache is PRIVATE and non-persistent (REDIS_PERSIST=no): it
#     starts empty and dies with the job, because the incrementality tests
#     assert real memoization and a cache outliving a test's stack poisons
#     them — unlike the registry, which is content-keyed and shared on purpose
#   - runnerd's docker client talks to the OUTER engine over the granted
#     socket, and each sibling joins THIS container's netns, so the inner
#     server on 127.0.0.1 is the address every worker already expects
#   - the server repo is SEEDED from $SEED, built above out of the std THIS
#     job was handed. The publisher is still the tree's own build-builtins.sh,
#     run once when the image was built (design/one-stack-image.md, "The
#     seed"); a test pays only for moving a few git objects, never a publish.
#
# Its registry settings need no overriding: this container sits on caos-net,
# so the default push URL (caos-registry:5000) is reachable here, and the
# default pull host (localhost:5000) is the name the OUTER docker daemon
# resolves — which is exactly the split this stack needs.
#
# It runs in the BACKGROUND because worker1 is what this job is for. serve
# dies as a group, so watching its pid is enough to know the stack is alive.
CAOS_STACK_STATE=/tmp/stack \
CAOS_STACK_LOGS=/tmp \
CAOS_STACK_READY=/tmp/stack.ready \
CAOS_STACK_BIN=/caos/bin \
CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PORT=6390 \
CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PERSIST=no \
CAOS_STACK_REGISTRY=no \
CAOS_STACK_RUNNERD=yes \
CAOS_STACK_SEED_GIT=$SEED \
CAOS_RUNNER_SLOTS=6 \
CAOS_PENDING_TIMEOUT_SECS=900 \
DOCKER_HOST="unix://$SOCK" \
CAOS_DOCKER_NETWORK="container:$(cat /etc/hostname)" \
  bash /caos/stack/serve >/tmp/serve.log 2>&1 &
SERVE=$!
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  [ -e /tmp/stack.ready ] && break
  kill -0 "$SERVE" 2>/dev/null || fail "the inner stack died during bring-up"
  sleep 1
done
[ -e /tmp/stack.ready ] || fail "the inner stack never came up"

# worker1 gets the inner stack; this script keeps the outer one. Everything
# it needs to talk to the stack above is set HERE and nowhere else.
PATH=/caos/bin:$PATH \
CAOS_SERVER_URL=$INNER \
CAOS_CLI=/caos/bin/caos-cli \
DOCKER_HOST="unix://$SOCK" \
  bash /cas/args/worker1

# The result, back under the OUTER environment: worker1 leaves its result
# tree at /tmp/out and this script publishes it. That is the contract here —
# unlike std/bash, worker1 does not `caos put /cas/out` itself, because it
# has no outer client to do it with.
if [ -e /tmp/out ]; then
  caos put /tmp/out /cas/out
elif [ ! -e /cas/out ]; then
  : > /tmp/caos-empty-out
  caos put /tmp/caos-empty-out /cas/out
fi
